monitoring: Inspect flowers and fruiting bodies regularly
Use approved pheromone traps for monitoring moth activity
prevention: Timely sowing to avoid late-season peaks
Strict crop residue management (destroy stalks after harvest)

early_signs: Yellow stripes of pustules on leaves
Yellow powder (spores) on fingers when rubbed
monitoring: Regular field scouting, especially in lower leaves and shady areas
Monitor regional weather advisories for high-humidity alerts
prevention: Sow recommended resistant varieties (e.g., PBW 826, Unnat PBW 343)
Avoid excessive use of nitrogenous fertilizers

early_signs: Yellowing and drying of plants in circular patches (Hopper burn)
Presence of small brown insects at the base of tillers
monitoring: Part the canopy and inspect the base of the stems near water level
Monitor weekly from maximum tillering to heading stage
prevention: Practice alternate wetting and drying (AWD) rather than continuous flooding

early_signs: Two parallel rings on the stem or petiole (Girdle Beetle)
Drooping and drying of terminal leaves
Tunneling inside the main stem (Stem Fly)
monitoring: Inspect plants 15-20 days after sowing for initial symptoms
prevention: Maintain optimum seed rate (do not over-seed)

early_signs: Presence of greenish-brown caterpillars on flowers and pods
monitoring: Install pheromone traps at the onset of flowering
Regularly inspect the upper canopy during flowering and pod formation stages
prevention: Install bird perches in the field to encourage natural predators
Intercropping with crops like sorghum or maize
Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae

early_signs: Damage to tender shoots and leaves
monitoring: Use pheromone traps starting from pre-flowering stage
Monitor crop weekly during flowering and pod development
prevention: Timely sowing is crucial to escape peak infestation
Mixed cropping with mustard or linseed
